skills.name: Copy a segment & an angle
skills.wrong_turn: Keep the compass width the same for matching arcs. Changing it between the original and the copy spoils the angle.
skills.rule: Copy a segment by carrying its length with the compass; copy an angle by copying a triangle inside it.

skills.name: Bisect a segment
skills.wrong_turn: If the compass is open less than half the segment, the arcs don't meet. Open it wider than halfway.
skills.rule: Equal arcs from A and B meet at two points; the line through them is the perpendicular bisector of AB.

skills.name: Bisect an angle
skills.wrong_turn: The bisector goes through the crossing of the second pair of arcs, not through where the first arc meets a side.
skills.rule: An arc from the vertex cuts both sides; equal arcs from those points cross; the ray to the crossing bisects the angle.

skills.name: Perpendicular through a point
skills.wrong_turn: Perpendicular doesn't mean vertical. It means meeting the given line at 90°, whichever way the line runs.
skills.rule: Mark two points of the line equally far from P, then build the perpendicular bisector between them.

skills.name: Parallel through a point
skills.wrong_turn: Copy the angle in the corresponding position, on the same side of the transversal. On the wrong side, the new line isn't parallel.
skills.rule: Through P, copy the angle a transversal makes with ℓ as a corresponding angle; the new line is parallel to ℓ.

skills.name: Triangle & hexagon in a circle
skills.wrong_turn: Don't change the compass after drawing the circle. The steps close up exactly only when each step equals the radius.
skills.rule: Stepping the radius around a circle gives a regular hexagon; alternate vertices give an equilateral triangle.

skills.name: Square in a circle
skills.wrong_turn: Joining the ends of two diameters makes a square only if they are perpendicular. Otherwise you get a rectangle.
skills.rule: Two perpendicular diameters meet the circle at the vertices of an inscribed square.

skills.name: Tangent from a point
skills.wrong_turn: The tangent doesn't touch where line OP crosses the circle. It touches where the radius meets it at a right angle.
skills.rule: The tangents from P touch the circle where the circle on diameter OP crosses it.

skills.name: Inscribed & circumscribed circles
skills.wrong_turn: The incenter comes from angle bisectors, not perpendicular bisectors. Perpendicular bisectors give the circumcenter, which can lie outside the triangle.
skills.rule: Perpendicular bisectors of the sides meet at the circumcenter; angle bisectors meet at the incenter.
